Phrased in the measure's own register; matching is by embedding similarity so a plain-language rewrite counts as recalled. 'essential' marks a provision a voter cannot make an informed choice without — severability and definitional clauses are deliberately not essential.

provisions.text: No insurer may delay, deny or modify a medical procedure or medication recommended by a treating physician where doing so could result in disability, death, amputation, permanent disfigurement, or loss or reduction of any bodily function.
A decision to delay, deny or modify care on behalf of an insurer may only be made by a physician.
In a lawsuit the insurer bears the burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence that the treatment was unnecessary or would not cause harm.
An insurer that wrongly delays, denies or modifies care is liable for treble damages and attorney fees.
Employing or conspiring to employ a non-physician to review a treating physician's decision is a felony.
Nothing in the section prevents the California Medical Board or Osteopathic Medical Board from imposing discipline.
Voters casting a ballot in person must present government-issued identification that conclusively verifies identity.
Elections officials may only count a regular or provisional ballot after verifying the voter's identity and that the person cast only one ballot.
The Secretary of State and county elections officials must maintain accurate voter registration lists and use best efforts to verify citizenship attestations against government data.
The state must provide a voter ID card free of charge to any eligible voter who requests one.
Counties must annually report the percentage of their voter rolls that have been citizenship-verified.
The State Auditor must audit state and county compliance during every odd-numbered year and report findings publicly.
The section is self-executing and the Legislature must enact implementing laws, including for military and overseas voters.

A state legislator who votes to propose or ratify a redistricting map, or to modify or suspend the redistricting process in effect on January 1 2025, becomes subject to the prohibitions that apply to redistricting commission members.
Such a legislator may not hold elective public office at federal, state, county or city level for ten years following that vote.
The penalty is triggered by any qualifying vote cast after January 1 2025.
A legislator already elected may serve out the remainder of that single term, but the ten-year bar then runs from the end of it.
Restores the right, lost in 2011, to vote on citizen-initiated ballot measures at statewide primary elections.
Amends Elections Code section 9016 to remove the restriction confining initiative and referendum measures to November general elections.
Retains a minimum interval between certification of a measure and the election at which it appears.
Beginning January 1 2027, no local government may impose, extend or increase any special tax unless it is submitted to the electorate and approved by a two-thirds vote.
The two-thirds requirement applies to the electorate of a local government exercising the initiative power, not only to the governing body.
No local government may impose ad valorem taxes on real property except as specifically provided.
'Local government' and 'special tax' carry the meanings already given in Article XIII C.
